story_type: diver with decompression sickness hoisted off a Coast Guard boat at speed
hook: A diver with the bends, hoisted off a speeding boat.
narration: Near Patos Island, Washington, this Coast Guard boat was carrying an injured diver, throwing up a wall of white water.
He had reportedly come down with decompression sickness.
When a diver comes up too fast, nitrogen dissolved in the body can form bubbles. Divers call it the bends.
A Dolphin helicopter from Air Station Port Angeles flew in above the forty-five foot response boat and lowered its basket to the deck.
The boat crew got him into the basket, and it swung clear of the wake.
At the door, the flight mechanic hauled him in.
outcome: The Dolphin crew hoisted the diver off the response boat and medevaced him.
title: Diver with the bends, hoisted at speed
description:
On Sept. 23, 2014, a Coast Guard Air Station Port Angeles helicopter crew hoisted a diver with reported decompression sickness off a 45-foot Coast Guard response boat near Patos Island, Washington.
